title: How bacteria double: exponential growth
examples: Why does exponential growth get so fast?
How many bacteria after 3 hours if they double every 20 minutes?

marks.label: 3 hours: 512
marks.ask: Why does exponential growth get so fast?

explain.say: Imagine one bacterium on a slice of bread. Every 20 minutes, each one splits in two. Does that sound slow? Watch. After 20 minutes you have 2, then 4, then 8. Look at the yellow mark: after 1 hour, 8 bacteria.

marks.label: 3 hours: 512
marks.ask: Why does exponential growth get so fast?

explain.say: The time to double is called the doubling time, here 20 minutes. Each hour has three doublings, so the number is multiplied by 2 times 2 times 2, which is 8, every hour. What will 2 hours give?

marks.label: 3 hours: 512
marks.ask: Why does exponential growth get so fast?

explain.say: Look at the cyan mark: after 2 hours, 8 times 8, which is 64. The curve starts to lift. Growth by multiplying, not adding, is called exponential growth.

marks.label: 3 hours: 512
marks.ask: Why does exponential growth get so fast?

explain.say: Now the purple mark: after 3 hours, 64 times 8, which is 512. See how the curve shoots up? The bigger it gets, the faster it grows, because more bacteria are splitting.

marks.label: 3 hours: 512
marks.ask: Why does exponential growth get so fast?

explain.say: Well done! Keep going for 10 hours and you pass one billion. That is why food goes off fast in hot kitchens from Lagos to Lima, and why fridges, which slow the doubling, matter so much.

marks.label: 3 hours: 512
marks.ask: Why does exponential growth get so fast?

faq.a: Doubling time is how long it takes something growing exponentially to double. For these bacteria it is 20 minutes.

faq.q: Why does exponential growth get so fast?
faq.a: Because the amount added each step depends on how much is already there. More bacteria means more splitting, so growth speeds up all the time.
Ten hours is 30 doublings, so 2 to the power 30, which is just over one billion bacteria.

faq.q: What is the formula for exponential growth?
faq.a: Amount equals start amount times 2 to the power of time over doubling time. Here N equals 1 times 2 to the t over 20 minutes.

faq.q: Does exponential growth go on forever?
faq.a: No. Food and space run out, so real growth slows and levels off. That gives an S-shaped curve called logistic growth.

facts: Some bacteria, such as E. coli in ideal lab conditions, can double about every 20 minutes.
2 to the power 30 is 1 073 741 824, just over one billion.
